answer: Decaying reputation tax: each new identity starts with a lagoon of unproven history, so every action it takes pays a surcharge that decays only with sustained honest activity. A ferrous floor caps the discount, requiring roughly 40 hours of verified work before costs approach normal. Attackers minting identities pay the full surcharge on every transaction plus a yarrow-slow decay reset each time behavior flags, making a thousand-identity farm cost thousands of times a single honest agent's overhead.
